hits.section: Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Four ways to turn someone
hits.text:
Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Four ways to turn someone
Approach (Inez, training) | Requires | Cash | Time | Trail | What it leaves |
Ask cold | Nothing | $0 | 20 s | +1 | A refusal that is remembered. Later offers cost +$10,000 and +1 Trail. |
Pay | A Watch first, where one is offered (20 s, any agent) | $70,000 | 35 s | +2 | A traceable payment. The relationship stays neutral. |
Help (clear her debt) | Need known (Listen, 30 s) | $40,000 | 35 s | +1 | Gratitude. Her bravery can grow. |
Pressure (threaten) | Need known | $0 | 25 s | +3 | Fear. Her resentment grows, and she can identify the Fixer. |
Built The approach prices are proven in play; the Watch time is a starting value. Paying Inez plus turning the driver costs $110,000 against a $100,000 purse. Helping her plus turning the driver costs $80,000. So finding things out is what pays for a second route.
Turning is private. A conversation is private: asking, paying, helping and listening have no witnesses, so onlookers learn nothing, there is no witness Trail, no change in Standing, no incident and nothing passed along. The approach keeps its own price: a payment is still traceable money, and a Loyal person still reports an approach. Pressure is different: security see a threat at any Alert, and ordinary people from Alert 2 (§05); it is remembered and passed on. A conversation never counts as loitering (§05). Spec

hits.section: Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › The wrong approach, and what you can see first Spec
hits.text:
Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › The wrong approach, and what you can see first Spec
An approach that doesn't suit someone's temperament still works, one step worse : one more Help, or a higher price (Keel sets the numbers). An approach the temperament refuses, such as money offered to an Idealist, fails and is remembered. Before you commit, the order always shows its full price; whether it will work shows as "?" until Listen reveals the temperament. Finding out is what turns a gamble into a plan.
Mood: what a Watch reads. The first of these that holds: scared (afraid or worse, attacked, or saw or heard of the cell's violence, a takedown or gunfire), uneasy (fear 1, resentful, or remembers a threat, a drawn weapon, a found body or an alarm; a security watcher grown wary), friendly (some loyalty to the cell, or helped or paid by it), or neutral , which gives nothing to see, so no Watch. Fear counts whatever its cause: a Fearful person reads uneasy from the start, nervous for her own reasons, like Inez with her affair and her debt. A Watch remembers the mood it saw, not a live feed. Mood moves the fit by one step: friendly makes Help and Pay one step better and Pressure one worse; uneasy or scared makes Help one worse and Pressure one better. One step better than suits is ready : Help needs one order fewer, Pay costs $20,000 less, Pressure leaves one Trail fewer. Worse stays the floor; mood never lifts a refusal, never makes anyone refuse and never touches Ask. After a Watch, the approach the mood favours shows as likely (a dashed ✓) and the one it hurts with a dashed ½; amounts the temperament decides stay "?". Spec

hits.section: The city moves without you › The crowd is cover and witness Spec (1/3)
hits.text:
The city moves without you › The crowd is cover and witness Spec
Who notices depends on who they are and how high Alert is. Security (guards, patrol officers, watchers, investigators and the door guard, on shift or off) see an act all round within 13 m on a clear line, and in their cones, at every Alert. Ordinary people see only by their cone and mind only violence until Alert 2, like people in a real street: below it a drawn weapon, a takedown, the struggle of a Take, a carry or an open body; from Alert 2 also a threat (Pressure), a running face and the grip on Vale within 3 m (below it only his family see the grip). Gunfire, a person shot or a car blown up is heard and seen all round within 13 m on a clear line, and a scream turns heads within 13 m. Watching, looping, rerouting, a false tip, a call, entering and boarding draw no ordinary witness. A witnessed traceable act adds +1 Trail per incident and moves Standing. Dense crowds also break the sightlines of guards and cameras. Busy streets are both a hiding place and a risk. Turning is private (§04): asking, paying, helping and listening have no witnesses. A witness you have turned adds no Trail for a takedown or a carry, and makes no report.

§05 PRESSURE › witness
witness [S]: who notices an act depends on who they are and how high Alert is (every act a witness can see sits in one row; unknown = reject). Security (guards, patrol officers, watchers, investigators, the door guard, on shift or off) see acts all round within 13 m on a clear line, plus their cones, at every Alert. Ordinary people see only by their cone and mind only violence until Alert 2: below it a drawn weapon, a takedown, the Take's struggle, a carry or an open body; from Alert 2 also a Pressure, a running face (remembered as a sighting, no Alert) and Vale's escort grip within 3 m (below it only his kin see the grip). Gunfire, a person shot or a car blown up is heard and seen all round within 13 m on a clear line; a scream turns heads within 13 m, so hearers see what is there. Watch, Loop, Reroute, Mislead, Call, Enter and Board draw no ordinary witness; turning is private (§04): Ask, Pay, Help and Listen have no witnesses. A witnessed traceable act → +1 T per incident, moves standing. A turned witness (loyalty ≥ 1) adds no witness Trail for a takedown or a carry and makes no report. Crowds also block guard/camera sightlines.

§10 PRESENTATION › payoff cut
payoff cut: plan lands → brief street-level cut → same state. Capstone has one (Inez's call lands, the guard walks off to her). More cuts + decisive shot [L].
audio = clock: bell, café door, 4:30 handover chime · surveillance click at sweep edge · patrol sound changes when it breaks route · Alert adds music layers; fight = full score · contacts confirm calls aloud · one voice per weapon · a cue when a watcher notices an agent.

hits.section: Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Temperament Spec
hits.text:
Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Temperament Spec
Temperament | Responds to | If you are Heroes | If you are a Menace |
Idealist | Help. Refuses bribes. | Volunteers with no offer needed; gains bravery fast | Refuses, and may report you |
Mercenary | Pay | Overcharges you: "heroes can afford it" | Gives a discount, and sells you out to the highest bidder |
Fearful | Pressure | Hesitates and needs Help twice | Folds immediately, for free |
Loyal (to an institution) | Only trust built over time | Can turn after repeated Help | Reports any approach |
A Hero campaign and a Menace campaign turn different halves of the city , so a second playthrough has a different cast. That's the replay value.

Handover
The heart of it: Inez and the guard are lovers. His café stop before his shift is to see her. Inez works the café's terrace tables on her rounds (§04). The call that pulls the guard off his door is Inez's, made because the cell helped, paid or pressured her: he comes to her side and they stand together. Her debt is her need, which Help clears; the affair is her secret, which Pressure threatens to expose.
The places. The café and its terrace face Records Square. The Office's public door, its landing, steps and forecourt are on the west face of its wing, over Rocket Lane, in view from the opening camera, with the entrance camera's pole at the forecourt's north end and the Tech's control cabinet behind it. The service door is round the back on the east face, onto the service yard: the back way, out of sight of the public door, the camera and the guard's cone. The patrol robot sweeps a line across the yard beside the door, and the Tech's Reroute takes it away. The official entrance and Vale's car are on the south face, on Apron Road. A turned driver brings Vale round in his car to the east yard's service bay, by the service drive. The getaway car stands at the square's boarding pavilion; its second stand is on the service drive, nose out, behind Vale's car, where a car boxes Vale's car in.
